body.statement: For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), the exact late-ramp construction satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, boundedness, predictable-randomization, intensity-profile, residual-profile, and profile-contract conditions for all sufficiently large \(n\). In particular, \(\bar q^{\sigma}\in\mathcal Q\), \(r^{\sigma}\in\mathcal R\), the profile errors vanish, the early rare-arm quadratic variation is eventually zero, and \(\tau_n^{+}-\tau_n^{-}\ge1/8\).
body.justification: The least-favorable witness must be shown to lie in the same declared adaptive class before it can support a uniform information bound.
body.gap: Existing adaptive-width lower bounds do not verify membership of this exact finite-population late-ramp pair with a completed propensity log.
body.consumer: The membership certificate makes the numerical lower-bound constant auditable against the proposal's maintained class.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\).  By \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair}, the potential outcomes and regressions are the deterministic arrays
\[
Y_{nt}^{\sigma}(0)=0,
\qquad
Y_{nt}^{\sigma}(1)=\sigma\delta _0\frac{(t/n-a_0)_+}{1-a_0},
\qquad
m_{nt}(0)=m_{nt}(1)=0 .
\]
They are therefore fixed under randomization, as required by \texttt{ass:fixed-outcomes}.  Since \(0\le (t/n-a_0)_+/(1-a_0)\le1\), \(\delta _0=1/4\), and \(M\ge\delta _0\),
\[
 |Y_{nt}^{\sigma}(a)|\le delta _0\le M
\]
for both arms, which verifies \texttt{ass:bounded-outcomes}.  The zero regression is \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\)-measurable and satisfies \(|m_{nt}(a)|=0\le M_m\), verifying \texttt{ass:predictable-regression} and \texttt{ass:bounded-regression}.

The assignment design in \texttt{ass:adaptive-assignment-law}, specialized by \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair}, has the deterministic predictable probabilities
\[
 \Pr_{\sigma}(A_{nt}=1\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=e_{nt}=\frac{c}{t}.
\]
Because \(c=1/2\), \(t\ge1\), and \(c\le\rho<1\),
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\frac{c}{t}\le c\le\rho<1,
\]
so \texttt{ass:propensity-range} also holds.

For the intensity profile, \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair} gives \(\bar q^{\sigma}(u)=c\).  Hence, for all \(u,v\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \bar q^{\sigma}(0)=c,
 \qquad
 \frac c2\le \bar q^{\sigma}(u)=c\le K,
 \qquad
 |\bar q^{\sigma}(u)-\bar q^{\sigma}(v)|=0\le L_q|u-v|.
\]
These are exactly the three membership conditions in \texttt{def:intensity-class}, and therefore \(\bar q^{\sigma}\in\mathcal Q\).  For the residual profile,
\[
 r^{\sigma}(u)=\sigma\delta _0\frac{(u-a_0)_+}{1-a_0}.
\]
The map \(u\mapsto(u-a_0)_+\) is one-Lipschitz.  Using \(B=M+M_m\ge M\ge\delta _0\) and \(L_r\ge\delta _0/(1-a_0)\), we obtain
\[
 |r^{\sigma}(u)|\le\delta _0\le B,
 \qquad
 |r^{\sigma}(u)-r^{\sigma}(v)|
 \le \frac{\delta _0}{1-a_0}|u-v|
 \le L_r|u-v|.
\]
Thus the two conditions in \texttt{def:residual-class} hold and \(r^{\sigma}\in\mathcal R\).

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the profile contract for this witness.  Write \(r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^{\sigma}(1)-m_{nt}(1)\), as in \texttt{def:good-event}.  For every \(n,t\), the two profile discrepancies in that definition are identically zero:
\[
 |t e_{nt}-\bar q^{\sigma}(t/n)|=|c-c|=0,
 \qquad
 |r_{nt}(1)-r^{\sigma}(t/n)|=0.
\]
Because \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is \(N_0\) such that \(\varepsilon_n< a_0=1/2\) for \(n\ge N_0\).  If \(n\ge N_0\) and \(t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\), then
\[
 \frac tn\le\frac{\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil-1}{n}<\varepsilon_n<a_0,
\]
and consequently \(r_{nt}(1)=r^{\sigma}(t/n)=0\).  Every summand of the early martingale in \texttt{def:good-event} is then zero, so
\[
 S_{n,\mathrm{rare}}^{\mathrm{early}}=0,
 \qquad
 \left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{rare}}^{\mathrm{early}}\right\rangle=0\le v_{0,n}.
\]
The moduli \(\delta_{q,n}\), \(\delta_{r,n}\), and \(v_{0,n}\) are nonnegative by their declared types.  Thus all three events defining \(G_n\) occur surely for \(n\ge N_0\), so \(G_n=\Omega\) and
\[
 \Pr_{\sigma}(G_n)=1\ge1-\kappa_n,
\]
because \(\kappa_n\ge0\).  This verifies \texttt{ass:profile-contract}; moreover, the two profile errors are exactly zero for every \(n\), and the early quadratic variation is exactly zero for all \(n\ge N_0\).

Finally, by the definition of \(\tau_n\), the control outcomes being zero, and the two signs in \texttt{def:late-ramp-pair},
\[
 \Delta_n:=\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-
 =\frac{2\delta _0}{1-a_0}\frac1n
   \sum_{t=1}^n(t/n-a_0)_+
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n(t/n-1/2)_+.
\]
If \(n=2m\), direct summation gives
\[
 \Delta_{2m}
 =\frac1{2m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{j}{2m}
 =\frac{m+1}{8m}\ge\frac18.
\]
If \(n=2m+1\), including \(m=0\), then
\[
 \Delta_{2m+1}
 =\frac{1}{2m+1}\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}
   \frac{2j-1}{2(2m+1)}
 =\frac{(m+1)^2}{2(2m+1)^2}>\frac18,
\]
where the last inequality follows from
\(4(m+1)^2-(2m+1)^2=4m+3>0\).  Hence \(\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-\ge1/8\) for every \(n\), which completes all asserted membership and separation claims.
